{{Short description|Concatenation of the first n prime numbers}}
{{pp-sock|small=yes}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Smarandache&ndash;Wellin number''' is an [[integer]] that in a given [[radix|base]] is the [[concatenation]] of the first ''n'' [[prime number]]s written in that base. Smarandache&ndash;Wellin numbers are named after [[Florentin Smarandache]] and [[Paul R. Wellin]].

The first [[decimal]] Smarandache–Wellin numbers are:

:[[2 (number)|2]], [[23 (number)|23]], [[235 (number)|235]], 2357, 235711, 23571113, 2357111317, 235711131719, 23571113171923, 2357111317192329, ... {{OEIS|id=A019518}}.

== Smarandache–Wellin prime ==
A Smarandache–Wellin number that is also prime is called a '''Smarandache–Wellin prime'''. The first three are 2, 23 and 2357 {{OEIS|id=A069151}}. The fourth is 355 digits long: it is the result of concatenating the first 128 prime numbers, through 719.<ref>{{cite book
  | last = Pomerance
  | first = Carl B.
  |author2=Crandall, Richard E.
   | author-link = Carl Pomerance
  | title = Prime Numbers: a computational perspective
  | publisher = Springer
  | year = 2001
  | pages = 78 Ex 1.86
  | isbn = 0-387-25282-7 }}
</ref>

The primes at the end of the concatenation in the Smarandache–Wellin primes are
:2, 3, 7, 719, 1033, 2297, 3037, 11927, ... {{OEIS|id=A046284}}.

The indices of the Smarandache–Wellin primes in the sequence of Smarandache–Wellin numbers are:
:1, 2, 4, 128, 174, 342, 435, 1429, ... {{OEIS|id=A046035}}.

The 1429th Smarandache–Wellin number is a prime with 5719 digits ending in 11927, discovered by [[Eric W. Weisstein]] as a [[probable prime]] in 1998<ref>Rivera, Carlos, [http://www.primepuzzles.net/puzzles/puzz_008.htm Primes by Listing]</ref> and then proven prime in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://factordb.com/index.php?id=1100000000534711999|access-date=2025-05-16|title=Primality proof of 2357111317...27|website=factordb.com}}</ref> In March 2009, Weisstein's search showed the index of the next Smarandache–Wellin prime (if one exists) is at least 22077.<ref>{{MathWorld|title=Integer Sequence Primes|urlname=IntegerSequencePrimes}} Retrieved 2011-07-28.</ref>
